chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Abbas ibn Amir, from Ali ibn Ma'mar, from Khalid Al-Qalanisi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'The Dhimmi (non-Muslim subject) meets me and shakes my hand.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Wipe it with dust and with the wall.' I said, 'And what about the Nasibi (Hostile one)?' He said: 'Wash it.'

key_terms.الذِّمِّيّ: Dhimmi, a non-Muslim living under Islamic rule
key_terms.النَّاصِب: Nasibi, one who is hostile or opposes the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wiping or washing the hand after shaking hands with a Dhimmi or Nasibi?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a nuanced jurisprudence of ritual purity (taharah) regarding physical contact with non-Muslims, distinguishing between the Dhimmi (protected non-Muslim) and the Nasibi (those hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt). The variation in purification—wiping with dust and wall for the Dhimmi versus washing for the Nasibi—reflects the Shia scholarly view that the nature of the contact and the status of the other party influence the degree of ritual impurity (najāsah) incurred. This ruling underscores the practical application of purity laws in daily social interactions within the early Islamic community.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kufy, from Abbas Bin Aamir, from Ali Bin Ma’mar, from Khalid Al Qalanasy who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘I met the Zimmy (Christian or Jew under the responsibility of the Islamic government), so he shook my hand’. Heasws said: ‘Wipe it with the dust and with the wall’. I said, ‘So (what about) the Nasibi (Hostile one)?’ Wash it’.
en.sarwar: 11. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Kufi from al-‘ Abbas ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mu’ammar from Khalid al-Qalanisi who has said the following:

“Once I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘What should I do if I meet a tax paying non-Muslim and he shakes my hand?’ The Imam said, ‘Wipe it with soil or against a wall.’ I asked, ‘What about one who is abusive of ‘A’immahV The Imam said, ‘Wash it (your hand).”’
